heading: Sec. 1-1. - How Code designated and cited.
toc_heading: Sec. 1-1. - How Code designated and cited.
path: Sec. 1-1. - How Code designated and cited.
text:
The provisions of this and the following chapters shall constitute and be designated
the "Code of Ordinances, City of Durham, North Carolina," which may also be cited
as the "Durham City Code," "City Code," "Code of the City of Durham," or phrase of
like nature.

(Code 1982, § 1-1)

State Law reference—
Codification required, G.S. 160A-77; admission into evidence of Code, G.S. 160A-79.

heading: Sec. 1-2. - Definitions and rules of construction.
toc_heading: Sec. 1-2. - Definitions and rules of construction.
path: Sec. 1-2. - Definitions and rules of construction.
text:
In the construction of this Code and of all ordinances and resolutions, the following
definitions and rules of construction shall be observed, unless inconsistent with
the manifest intent of the council or the context clearly requires otherwise. This
section is subject to section 1-10.

Charter. The term "Charter" means the Charter of the City of Durham, North Carolina.

City, municipality. The terms "city" and "municipality" mean the City of Durham, in the State of North
Carolina. Where the context admits, it shall mean the city manager.

Code. The terms "the Code" and "this Code" mean the Code of Ordinances, City of Durham,
North Carolina, as designated in section 1-1.

Computation of time. The time within which an act is to be done shall be computed by excluding the day
of the act, event, default or publication after which the designated period of time
begins to run and including the last day; unless the last day is a Saturday, Sunday
or legal holiday, in which event the period runs until the end of the next day which
is not a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday. When the period of time prescribed or
allowed is less than seven days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays
shall be excluded in the computation. A half holiday shall be considered as other
days and not as a legal holiday.

Conjunctions. Conjunctions, such as "and" and "or," shall each be deemed to include the other as
the context shall admit.

Council, governing body. The terms "council," "city council," and "governing body" mean the city council of
the City of Durham.

County. The term "county" means the County of Durham, in the State of North Carolina. Where
the pertinent location is not in the County of Durham, the applicable county is intended.

Day, business day, working day. The term "day" means a calendar day. The terms "business day" and "working day" are
equivalent to each other and exclude weekends and legal holidays. This definition
is subject to the definition of "computation of time" above.

Examples. The principle that the expression of one thing is the exclusion of another will not
alone generally be sufficient to override the presumption that the provisions of this
chapter are to be used to construe all ordinances. For instance, if an ordinance twice
uses the word "includes," and at one of those occasions it modifies that use with
the phrase "but is not limited to," the presumption will still stand that the definition
of "include" in this section 1-2 applies to the other use of "includes" in that ordinance.

G.S., General Statutes. The abbreviation "G.S." and the expression "General Statutes," mean the General Statutes
of North Carolina.

Gender. Words importing one gender include the other genders.

Governmental person. The term "governmental person" means government and an agency, subdivision, or unit
of government, such as a city, town, county, board of education, sanitary district,
airport authority, state, and the federal government. Depending on the context, the
term may include the City of Durham.

Holiday. A "holiday" is a day observed by city government as a holiday or legal holiday as
provided in section 42-16(a), (b).

Include. The term "include" and its various forms are used without limitation.

Joint authority. All words giving a joint authority to three or more persons or officers shall be
construed as giving such authority to a majority of such persons or officers.

Law, statute, rule, regulation, code.

(a)

Where an ordinance or resolution incorporates by reference a law, statute, rule, regulation,
standard, or code adopted by any person other than the city council, the law, statute,
rule, regulation, standard, or code in effect on the date of adoption by the city
council of the ordinance or resolution is incorporated.

(b)

Where the City Code as adopted in the 2008 recodification incorporates by reference
a law, statute, rule, regulation, standard, or code adopted by any person other than
the city council, subsection (a) of this definition shall not apply. Instead, the
law, statute, rule, regulation, standard, or code in question is incorporated as it
was in effect of the date of the adoption of the ordinance adopting the 2008 recodification.

(c)

References in ordinances and resolutions that are intended to call attention to laws,
statutes, rules, regulations, standards, and codes, but which are not intended to
incorporate by reference, are not subject to subsections (a) and (b) of this definition.

Legal holiday. A "legal holiday" is a day observed by city government as a holiday or legal holiday
as provided in section 42-16(a), (b).

Manager, city manager. The term "manager" or "city manager" means the city manager of the City of Durham
and his or her designee.

Month. The term "month" means a calendar month.

Number. Words used in the singular include the plural and the plural includes the singular
number.

Oath. The term "oath" includes an affirmation in all cases in which, by law, an affirmation
may be substituted for an oath, and in such cases the terms "swear" and "sworn" are
equivalent to the terms "affirm" and "affirmed."

Officer. Reference to an officer by title includes any duly authorized deputy or assistant
of such officer, or, to the extent allowed by law, the agent of such officer.

Officer, department, board, etc. Reference to an officer, department, board or other entity by title refers to the
officer, department, board, etc., of the city in contrast with an officer, department,
board, etc., of any other entity.

Ordinance. The term "ordinance" includes ordinances contained in this Code and ordinances omitted
from this Code.

Owner. The term "owner," applied to a building or land, includes any part owner, joint owner,
tenant in common, joint tenant or tenant by the entirety, of the whole or a part of
such building or land.

Person:

(1)

The term "person" includes an individual, corporation, limited liability company,
firm, partnership, association, organization, any group acting as a unit, and governmental
person. The use of the term "person" in the ordinances and in resolutions, where either
is adopted after the date of the adoption of the 2007 recodification of the City Code,
is as stated in this subsection (1).

(2)

The use of the term "person" in ordinances and in resolutions, where either was adopted
on or before the date of the adoption of the 2007 recodification of the City Code,
shall be construed without consideration of subsection (1) of this definition.

Personal property. The term "personal property" includes every species of property except real property.

Preceding, following. The terms "preceding" and "following" mean next before and next after, respectively.

Property. The term "property" includes real and personal property.

Real property. The term "real property" includes lands, tenements and hereditaments.

Registered mail. The term "registered mail" includes certified mail.

Religious facility. The expression "religious facility" means a building or structure, and any appurtenance
thereof, where the building or structure is primarily used or designated by a non-profit
organization for religious observance, services, worship, or instruction.

Shall, may. The term "shall" is mandatory; the term "may" is permissive.

Sidewalk. The term "sidewalk" means any portion of a street between the curbline and the adjacent
property line intended for the use of pedestrians.

Signature. The term "signature" includes a mark when the person cannot write.

State. The term "state" means the State of North Carolina.

Street. The term "street" includes any public way, road, highway, street, avenue, boulevard,
parkway, alley, lane, viaduct, and bridge and the approaches thereto, which has been
accepted for maintenance by the state or by the city.

Tenant, occupant. The terms "tenant" and "occupant," applied to a building or land, include any person
who leases or occupies, respectively, the whole or a part of such building or land,
whether alone or with others.

Time. Words used in the past, present or future tense each include the other tenses.

UDO, Unified Development Ordinance. The term "UDO" means the Unified Development Ordinance. Unless the context indicates
otherwise, UDO and Unified Development Ordinance refer to the Unified Development
Ordinance of the city, rather than of the county.

Weekdays, weekend. "Weekdays" are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. The "weekend" is
Saturday and Sunday.

Writing. The terms "writing" and "written" includes printing and any other visual mode of
representing words and letters.

Year. The term "year" means a calendar year in contrast to a fiscal or other year. However,
in some contexts the term "year" means the period of time between two dates such that
they are one year apart. For instance, "during the two years before January 15, 2006"
will generally mean January 15, 2004 through January 14, 2006 instead of January 1,
2004 through December 31, 2005.

(Code 1982, § 1-2; Ord. No. 13574, Pt. 1, 4-7-2008)

State Law reference—
Similar definitions and rules of statutory construction, G.S. 12-3, 160A-1; computation
of time, G.S. 1-593 (Rules of Civ. Proc., Rule 6(a)).

heading: Sec. 1-3. - Supplementation of Code; ordinances of limited interest or transitory nature; setting fees.
toc_heading: Sec. 1-3. - Supplementation of Code; ordinances of limited interest or transitory nature; setting fees.
path: Sec. 1-3. - Supplementation of Code; ordinances of limited interest or transitory nature; setting fees.
text:
(a)

By contract or by municipal personnel, supplements to this Code shall be prepared
and printed whenever authorized or directed by the city. A supplement to the Code
shall include all substantive permanent and general parts of ordinances passed by
the city council during the period covered by the supplement and all changes made
thereby in the Code, and such supplement may also include amendments to the Charter.
The pages of a supplement shall be so numbered that they will fit properly into the
Code and will, where necessary, replace pages which have become obsolete or partially
obsolete, and the new pages shall be so prepared that, when they have been inserted,
the Code will be current through the date of the adoption of the latest ordinance
included in the supplement.

(b)

In preparing a supplement to this Code, all portions of the Code which have been repealed
shall be excluded from the Code by the omission thereof from reprinted pages.

(c)

When preparing a supplement to this Code, the codifier (meaning the person authorized
to prepare the supplement) may make formal, nonsubstantive changes in ordinances and
parts of ordinances included in the supplement, insofar as it is necessary to do so
to embody them into a unified code. For example, the codifier may:

(1)

Organize the ordinance material into appropriate subdivisions;

(2)

Provide appropriate catchlines, headings and titles for sections and other subdivisions
of the Code printed in the supplement, and make changes in such catchlines, headings
and titles;

(3)

Assign appropriate numbers to sections and other subdivisions to be inserted in the
Code and, where necessary to accommodate new material, change existing section or
other subdivision numbers;

(4)

Change the words "this ordinance" or words of the same meaning to "this chapter,"
"this article," "this division," etc., as the case may be, or to "sections _______
to _______" (inserting section numbers to indicate the sections of the Code which
embody the substantive sections of the ordinance incorporated into the Code); and

(5)

Make other nonsubstantive changes necessary to preserve the original meaning of ordinance
sections inserted into the Code; but, in no case, shall the codifier make any change
in the meaning or effect of ordinance material included in the supplement or already
embodied in the Code.

(d)

The following ordinances, including ordinances renewing, extending, or amending such
ordinances, are not to be codified:

(1)

Ordinances that set dates, times, or locations of regular city council meetings, including
work session meetings, when all of such meetings will occur within 13 months of the
adoption of the ordinance.

(2)

Ordinances that will have no effect after 13 months from the adoption of the ordinance.

(3)

Ordinances that promise or guarantee the payment of money by or for the city, or authorize
the issuance of bonds of the city or evidence of the city's indebtedness.

(4)

Ordinances that authorize a contract or the assumption of an obligation by the city.

(5)

Ordinances that make an appropriation.

(6)

Ordinances that provide for local improvements or that impose assessments therefor.

(7)

Ordinances that accept a plat or subdivision.

(8)

Ordinances that change the boundaries of the city.

(9)

Ordinances that set the rate for ad valorem property taxes.

(10)

Capital project ordinances and grant project ordinances.

(11)

Ordinances that name streets.

(12)

Budget ordinances.

(e)

The following ordinances, including ordinances renewing, extending, or amending such
ordinances, are to be codified as technical ordinances and shall be published separately
from this Code:

(1)

Franchises granted pursuant to section 67 et seq. of the Charter or pursuant to G.S.
160A-76.

(2)

Ordinances that set tax rates, except for ad valorem property taxes and privilege
license taxes.

(3)

The emergency operations plan adopted pursuant to section 22-21.

(4)

The Unified Development Ordinance.

(f)

The following ordinances, including ordinances renewing, extending, or amending such
ordinances, shall be codified by entry upon official lists or schedules:

(1)

Ordinances that set rates for utility or other public enterprise services.

(2)

Ordinances that set fees to be charged by the city.

(3)

Ordinances that set fares, rates, and charges that may be charged by passenger vehicles
for hire.

(4)

Except to the extent the city council otherwise provides, and except as provided in
other subsections of this section, ordinances that regulate or set any rates, deposits,
fees, fares, and charges imposed by any person, including the city, and including
credits granted by the city; provided, however, that ordinances setting a charge that
is denominated as a "civil penalty" will be in this Code instead of on an official
list or schedule.

(g)

Unless provided otherwise, fees referred to in ordinances will be set by the city
council from time to time.

(h)

The technical ordinances referred to in subsection (e)(2) and the official lists and
schedules referred to in subsection (f) are referred to in this subsection as the
"fee schedule." From time to time the city manager shall, in consultation with the
city attorney, prepare and revise the fee schedule as appropriate to accurately reflect
decisions by the city council regarding fees, fares, rates, charges, etc. set by such
technical ordinances and official lists and schedules (referred to collectively as
"fee schedule charges"). The intent is that the fee schedule is to be kept current
to show fee schedule charges in effect when the schedule is revised. In general, repealed
fee schedule charges shall be removed from the schedule, but in the city manager's
discretion historical information may be provided in the fee schedule if it is labeled
or arranged so that readers are not likely to be confused regarding which schedule
charges are in effect. Without limiting the foregoing authority, the city manager
may make non-substantive changes to decisions by the city council, insofar as it is
necessary to do so to embody them in the fee schedule. For example, the city manager
may in consultation with the city attorney:

(1)

Reorganize the material into appropriate subdivisions, including parts, sections,
and chapters, including designating which departments, divisions, offices, etc. are
primarily responsible for particular schedule charges.

(2)

Assign and change captions.

(3)

Assign and change numbers of subdivisions.

(4)

Write and change references to ordinances, resolutions, chapters, sections, articles,
divisions, etc. to communicate the meaning of the council's decisions being embodied
in the schedule.

(5)

Make other non-substantive changes as necessary to preserve the meaning of the council's
decisions being embodied in the schedule.

(Code 1982, § 1-3; Ord. No. 13574, Pt. 1, 4-7-2008; Ord. No. 13575, § 4, 4-7-2008;
Ord. No. 14415, § 1, 4-1-2013; Ord. No. 14416, § 1, 4-1-2013)

State Law reference—
Code of Ordinances, G.S. 160A-77.

Reorganize the material into appropriate subdivisions, including parts, sections, and chapters, including designating which departments, divisions, offices, etc. are primarily responsible for particular schedule charges.

(2)

Assign and change captions.

(3)

Assign and change numbers of subdivisions.

(4)

Write and change references to ordinances, resolutions, chapters, sections, articles, divisions, etc. to communicate the meaning of the council's decisions being embodied in the schedule.

(5)

Make other non-substantive changes as necessary to preserve the meaning of the council's decisions being embodied in the schedule.

(Code 1982, § 1-3; Ord. No. 13574, Pt. 1, 4-7-2008; Ord. No. 13575, § 4, 4-7-2008; Ord. No. 14415, § 1, 4-1-2013; Ord. No. 14416, § 1, 4-1-2013)

State Law reference— Code of Ordinances, G.S. 160A-77.
